_doc: Cross-language RENDER contract: formats that must look identical wherever a user meets them, across Python (CLI + server), TypeScript (React SPA) and Swift (macOS). Sibling of pipeline-summary-contract.json, which does the same job for PARSED contracts — see docs/design-shared-formats.md for the distinction and for why it matters which kind you are holding. Established 22 Aug 2026.
_how_to_use: Each entry carries a `status`. `aligned` entries are ASSERTED by tests/test_shared_format_contract.py and frontend/src/utils/sharedFormatContract.test.ts — their `cases` are the agreed truth and a drifting implementation fails its own suite. `divergent` entries are CATALOGUED ONLY: no test asserts their `observed` values as correct, because they are not. They record measured reality so the gap is visible and countable. Closing a gap means moving the entry to `aligned` in the same commit as the fix.
_not_a_codegen_step: Deliberately hand-maintained, matching the stance in tests/test_swift_contract_parity.py. These are five-line functions doing integer division; a schema compiler in three toolchains would cost more than the drift it prevents. Revisit if a fourth language appears.

duration_human.datum: An elapsed span — how long a session ran. NOT a position in a recording (see `timecode`).

implementations.python: bristlenose/server/routes/dashboard.py::_format_duration_human — feeds the duration_human and total_duration_human API fields
implementations.typescript: frontend/src/utils/format.ts::formatDurationHuman — Sessions grid, Dashboard session table, Sessions sidebar
implementations.swift: desktop/Bristlenose/Bristlenose/DurationFormat.swift::DurationFormat.human — window subtitle, sessions popover, cloud import list

divergences.why: Python and Swift format aggregate TOTALS, where a real zero is a real answer. The TypeScript sites format a per-row CELL, where zero means the duration is unknown — 19 of 236 sessions in the local trial corpus (8%) — and '0m' would assert a measurement nobody made. The em-dash is the SPA's established convention for an absent cell value, shared with formatFinderDate and formatCompactDate. Excluded from `cases` above because there is no single right answer; each side is right for its own context.

duration_human.notes: The h/m abbreviations are knowingly unlocalised on all three sides. Changing that is a separate decision with a 22-locale cost — see docs/design-shared-formats.md.

timecode.datum: A POSITION in a recording — where a quote sits. NOT an elapsed span (see `duration_human`).
timecode.decision: 22 Aug 2026 (Martin): pad the MINUTE field, never the HOUR field. Minutes genuinely range 00-59, so padding buys column alignment across a list of quotes. Hours never reach two digits in research data — the longest session in ten years of the maintainer's practice is 90 minutes, and an all-morning symposium tops out near 3h — so padding the hour reserves a column for '09:34:23' that no interview will ever occupy, and makes the reader parse a leading zero that is meaningless 99% of the time. It also matches how video editors render elapsed position, which is the tool researchers use to trim clips from these same recordings. Sub-minute timecodes are explicitly out of scope as a real-world case.

implementations.python: bristlenose/utils/timecodes.py::format_timecode — the only Python implementation. Re-exported from models.py for the stages that import it there; export_core.py and mcp_server.py import it directly.
implementations.typescript: frontend/src/utils/format.ts::formatTimecode — the only TypeScript implementation. Imported by exportActions.ts, AppLayout.tsx, ProposalZoneList.tsx and AutoCodeReportModal.tsx, which each held a private copy until 22 Aug 2026.
implementations.swift: none — the Mac surfaces that show a position go through the SPA.

divergences.typescript: 59:50 (no clamp; JS modulo on a negative)
divergences.why: Not reachable from real data — a timecode is a position in a recording and cannot be negative — so this is a latent difference in defensive behaviour rather than a live bug, and is excluded from `cases` rather than fixed. If a clamp is ever added to the TypeScript side, add the case here and it becomes enforced.

timecode.notes: Was 9 implementations across 3 formats until 22 Aug 2026; 8 were copy-paste duplicates of a helper that already existed in the same language. The user-visible symptom was a quote card rendering 05:30 while the CSV export of that same quote rendered 5:30.
timecode.also_parsed: UNLIKE every other entry here, this format has a PARSED half. Transcript .txt/.md files are a round-trip format — the pipeline writes them with format_timecode and reads them back on resume and re-analysis via the regex at bristlenose/pipeline.py (search 'Parse transcript lines'). So timecode is Class R on screen and Class W on disk. Consequences: (1) the reader's leading field must stay `\d{1,2}` — it was `\d{2}` until 22 Aug 2026 and a `[1:00:00]` segment was then dropped SILENTLY, no error, a short transcript the only symptom; (2) that tolerance is permanent backward compatibility, because transcripts already on researchers' disks carry the old `[01:00:00]` form. Both directions are pinned in tests/test_transcript_writing.py (test_parser_mixed_timecode_formats and test_parser_still_reads_legacy_zero_padded_hours). Before changing a rendered format, check whether anything parses it back.

finder_filename.datum: A filename truncated Finder-style with a middle ellipsis, default budget 24 chars.
finder_filename.decision: 22 Aug 2026: round the 2:1 front/back split UP, adopting the TypeScript form. The two sides used the same ratio and differed only in rounding — floor in Python, ceil in TypeScript — so they disagreed for every 3-, 4- and 6-character extension (i.e. every common media file) and agreed only on 2- and 5-character ones. Neither lost information; the difference was one character of balance. TypeScript won because it is the live surface — the Sessions grid and Dashboard filename column — while the Python side feeds only the sealed static render and the dev route, so adopting it changed nothing any user sees. It is also the front-heavier form, which is what the Python docstring said it wanted.

implementations.python: bristlenose/utils/markdown.py::format_finder_filename — sealed static render (s12_render/dashboard.py) and the dev route (server/routes/dev.py)
implementations.typescript: frontend/src/utils/format.ts::formatFinderFilename — Sessions grid and Dashboard filename column; the live surface

finder_filename.notes: Verified by exhaustive sweep: 472 synthetic names (extension lengths 0-7 x stem lengths 1-59) plus the real trial-corpus filenames, zero mismatches. The Python docstring's worked example was ALSO wrong before this — it claimed 'Fishkeeping Rese...S3.vtt', an output neither implementation ever produced, and was corrected in the same commit. The character budget is itself an approximation: Finder truncates by pixel width with NSLineBreakByTruncatingMiddle, not by character count, so this matches Finder's shape rather than its arithmetic.

finder_date.datum: A timestamp rendered the way Finder renders relative dates: Today / Yesterday / absolute.

implementations.swift: desktop/Bristlenose/Bristlenose/SessionsFinderDate.swift::SessionsFinderDate.format — sessions popover subtitle; a deliberate mirror of the TS contract

divergences.why: The TS/Swift pair is at exact parity because the popover and the grid sit on the same lens and must agree. The Python rendering targets a markdown transcript header, a different medium, and uses ' at ' as its separator. SessionsFinderDate.swift documents this explicitly and adopts the TypeScript contract by name.

finder_date.notes: Not machine-pinned: all three take a clock and a locale, so a fixture would need injected time and an Intl/CLDR-stable locale on three runtimes. The Swift header (SessionsFinderDate.swift:1-46) is the exemplar contract docstring in this codebase — read it before writing a new mirror. Its KNOWN-WRONG section also records that the underlying VALUE is questionable (st_birthtime, not session start), which is a data problem rather than a format one and is tracked separately.

implementations.typescript: i18next CLDR plurals via t(key, {count}) — React SPA

plural_category.gap: None — three mechanisms by design, already documented in the root CLAUDE.md i18n section. Listed here only so a future reader does not 'discover' it and try to unify it.
